A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Through the Valley. All 20 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison. Relocated related work and renumbered appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections 2–4 report original fine-tuning experiments, reflection analysis, synthetic arithmetic evaluations and downstream reinforcement-learning results, with additional results and examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Sections 2–4 and the appendices, including model-scaling comparisons, synthetic arithmetic evaluations and reinforcement-learning outcomes.

M1.justification: The full-parameter SFT procedure, conditional log-likelihood objective, GRPO algorithm with correctness rewards, and keyword/GPT-4o-mini reflection identification remain unchanged. The additions describe existing procedures rather than introduce method components.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenR1-Math-220k for SFT, MATH subsets for RL, and AIME24, AMC23, MATH500 and the same synthetic arithmetic benchmark for evaluation. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated models and comparison groups are unchanged. In particular, Figure 7 retains the same Base, 8k and 128k SFT-initialization comparisons; newly cited works are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Training subset sizes, model configurations, Tables 2–3 hyperparameters, decoding settings and synthetic evaluation procedures are retained. Section 2.2 newly explains response length and the accuracy/length interpretation of token efficiency, which were already discussed in v1; it does not establish a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The reflection-frequency and response-length analyses, controlled arithmetic error analysis, and qualitative examples are unchanged. The corresponding material in v1 Appendices B–C is retained in v2 Appendices A–B without new ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Both retain the same sampled-response averaging and reported response counts. Neither adds training-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The empirical accuracy, response-length and reflection curves are unchanged, including the detailed benchmark results in Figures 11–12. Figures 6 and 13–15 retain the same qualitative outputs. No measured result entries are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical description of SFT is unchanged. Despite its title, new Section 5.2 provides conceptual research context rather than formal assumptions, derivations or proofs. The token-efficiency ratio explains an existing concept rather than introduces new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: identifying Long CoT Degradation, attributing it to verbose reasoning and accumulated errors, and showing the downstream RL benefits of sufficiently scaled SFT.

C2.justification: Section 2.3 now connects incomplete recovery to a learnability gap. New Section 5.2 distinguishes degradation from catastrophic forgetting and relates it to other non-monotonic learning dynamics. The limitations add uncertainty about generalization beyond autoregressive models, while removing some discussion of future work and non-mathematical training-data availability.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly identifies the official Qwen2.5-Math evaluation repository, supplies its link, and describes UltraEval with vLLM-based multi-GPU data-parallel inference. The hardware, training-time estimates and hyperparameter tables were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: New Section 5.2 adds focused positioning relative to catastrophic forgetting, domain adaptation, modality shifts and deep double descent, with corresponding citations. Overthinking and evaluation-software references are also added. Much of the expanded main-text related work is relocated from v1 Appendix A; publication updates concern existing works.

P1.justification: The short main-text related-work summary is replaced by the detailed appendix discussion, organized into Sections 5.1 and 5.3 around new Section 5.2. Other edits include metric explanations, revised limitations, appendix renumbering and updated affiliations/contact information. Most scientific prose is retained.

P2.justification: Both retain the same 15 figures and three tables without substantive graphic redesign. There are limited placement and spacing changes: Figure 4 moves to the top of the right column, and appendix figures and tables shift with the reorganized text. Caption cross-references are updated.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility by identifying the evaluation software and repository, and improves clarity through metric explanations and the explicit architecture limitation. The empirical evidence remains unchanged. The added context is useful, although Section 5.2's claim of monotonic recovery overstates some retained curves, such as Qwen2.5-1.5B in Figure 2. This local overstatement limits, but does not outweigh, the documentation gains.
